video.title: How a Regular Guy Started a 1-Person Business with AI

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Phil, a semi-retiree with no coding background who started an AI agency after listening to the podcast. Phil landed a $50,000 six-month retainer with a $1.4B investment firm, a success-based grant-writing app (Grant Craft) for a nonprofit, and a $3,500 + $1,500/month product-launch automation deal for a chiropractor, all from friends and friends of friends. He records discovery meetings and uses Claude for solutions, pricing and contracts, building in Go High Level and Claude Code. Key takeaways: sell to your warm network, listen more than talk, ask for referrals, and productise custom builds.

speakers.name: Phil
speakers.description: Phil (Philip), semi-retired, runs a one-person AI automation agency

ideas.name: Part-time AI automation consultant selling to warm network
ideas.one_liner: A retiree with no coding background sells AI automations and content systems to friends and friends-of-friends, landing a $50k six-month retainer with an investment firm.
ideas.customer: Small and mid-sized business owners in his personal network (investment firm managing $1.4B, chiropractor, nonprofit)
ideas.problem: Owners know they need AI but don't know where to start or how
ideas.offer: Custom AI automations, voice agents, and knowledge-base content creation built with Claude/Claude Code and Go High Level

pricing.notes: Client proposed the $50k figure after Phil asked how many hours a week he wanted.

acquisition_channels.details: Texted 1,000+ phone contacts asking to sit down; 7-10 meetings with business owners. In the UK, texting personal contacts you know is lower risk but unsolicited marketing SMS to individuals needs consent under PECR.

quote.text: I basically went through all of the contacts on my phone. I've got more than a thousand contacts and I just started making a list and just started sending texts
quote.speaker: Phil

acquisition_channels.details: Cold-called roofing companies early with voice agents; little success.

ideas.delivery: Phil records discovery conversations, feeds transcripts to Claude to design solutions, price and draft contracts, then builds in Go High Level/Claude Code.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: About 5 months from starting (Oct) to first $50k contract (March)

onboarding.how: Discovery meetings are human; AI helps prepare.

delivery.how: AI builds much of it but custom work needs a human.

uk_applicability.notes: AI consulting works the same in the UK; warm outreach fine, cold SMS to individuals restricted by PECR.

risks: Hard to scale beyond friends and family

quotes.text: the contract that he gave me for the first six months will renew after six month months was for $50,000
quotes.speaker: Phil

quotes.text: Every bit of the business that I have had to this point has been from people from either direct contacts, direct friends or friends of friends
quotes.speaker: Phil

ideas.name: Grant Craft: AI grant finder and drafter for nonprofits
ideas.one_liner: App that finds grants matching a nonprofit, researches requirements and drafts applications for human review; priced as success-based retainer.
ideas.business_model: Per-grant fee plus retainer, billed only when a grant is won, capped at 8% of the grant
ideas.problem: Finding and writing grant applications is time-consuming
ideas.offer: Automated grant discovery and drafting, human review before submission

pricing.notes: No billing until a grant comes through; total billing capped at 8% of the grant.

acquisition_channels.details: Built free for a friend's nonprofit as proof of concept.

ideas.delivery: Claude Code app plus an OpenClaw agent fills out grant applications; human reads before sending.
unit_economics_claims: $1,500 per grant + $2,000/month, capped at 8% of grant
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Not until a grant is awarded

acquisition.how: Grant-seeking nonprofits can be reached by content/SEO; UK charities are often companies (CIOs/charitable companies) so B2B email may be possible.

onboarding.how: Feed knowledge base about the organisation.

delivery.how: Agent finds and drafts grants; human review before submission.

uk_applicability.notes: UK has many grant funders and charities; success fees for bid writing are debated ethically by some funders.

risks: Some funders disallow commission-based grant writing

quotes.text: I'll charge you $1,500 per grant that I fill out, $2,000 a month for the retainer for the service. However, I will not bill you anything till until you have a grant come through
quotes.speaker: Phil

ideas.name: Done-for-you product launch for a chiropractor's laser service
ideas.one_liner: Set up content creation, a GHL bot sent to 7,500 existing clients, sign-up forms and monthly social management to launch a body-toning laser.
ideas.business_model: Setup fee plus monthly retainer plus per-client bonus
ideas.customer: Chiropractor/clinic owner launching a new service
ideas.problem: Owner doesn't know how to launch and market the new laser
ideas.offer: Content app, client Q&A bot, sign-up forms, social media management

pricing.notes: Client also pays CRM costs and $500/month ad budget.

acquisition_channels.details: Came from the Grant Craft friend (who is a chiropractor).

ideas.delivery: Built in Go High Level in ~12 hours; ~1.5 hours/month ongoing.

delivery.how: Content generation and bot automated after setup.

uk_applicability.notes: Works in UK; messaging existing clients needs prior consent (soft opt-in) under PECR; medical/aesthetic advertising rules (ASA/CAP) apply.

tactics.name: Warm-network AI agency launch
steps: Go through every phone contact and list business owners
Text: I've started an AI automation business, I'd love to sit down with you
Let them talk about pain points; don't pitch features
Feed transcript into Claude for solutions, pricing, contract and objection prep

quote.text: Hey, I've started this AI automation business, You know, I'd love to be able to sit down with you
quote.speaker: Phil

tactics.name: Record discovery calls and analyse with AI
steps: Use a wearable (Limitless/Plaud) or phone voice notes
Generate solutions, pricing and contract drafts

tactics.name: Success-based pricing for proof of concept
steps: Cap total at a % of outcome

tactics.name: Setup + retainer + performance bonus structure
steps: Client pays CRM and $500/month ad budget

tactics.name: Let the client name the retainer
steps: Ask how many hours a week they want
Throw in automations free inside the retainer

tactics.name: Floodgate principle
steps: Solve one problem for a friend

tools_mentioned.name: Claude Code
tools_mentioned.purpose: Building apps such as Grant Craft

warnings.warning: Talking too much and listing AI features lost most early prospects.

quote.text: my first encounters with them looking back involved me talking too much sharing all the things that AI would do rather than letting them share the challenges
quote.speaker: Phil

warnings.warning: Can't scale only on friends and family; need to branch out.

quote.text: I don't believe you can you can only scale with friends and family
quote.speaker: Phil

warnings.warning: MLM-style list-everyone-you-know selling burns relationships if the product is bad.
Hiding what you're working on from friends creates an artificial sales barrier.
Texting your whole contact list is marketing: in the UK PECR requires consent for marketing SMS to individuals.

lessons.lesson: Start with people you know; warm leads close far better than cold calls.

quote.text: a friend of a friend is light years better than a cold call
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: The best selling is listening; let owners describe pain points.
You only need to know more than 99% of the owners you sit with.

quote.text: 99% of the business owners that we sit in front of, we know significantly more than they do
quote.speaker: Phil

lessons.lesson: Revenue matters more than having a niche early.

quote.text: you have revenue, right? And that's that's more valuable than a niche
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Content for local businesses is now like a sign: a basic presence, not virality.
Custom builds for one business can become vertical products for the whole industry.
Always ask for referrals after delivering.
Close the big deal then figure out delivery: get a bigger frying pan.
Talk to yourself as you would to your kids; don't voice negative thoughts.

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand deal terms are specific, but few clients and early-stage; the $833/month figure conflicts with $50k/6 months.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Chris promotes his Playmakers AI agency community; Beehiiv sponsor read.
